'''Northwestern Tasmanian''', or '''Peerapper''' ("Pirapa"), is an [[Aboriginal Tasmanian|Aboriginal language]] of [[Tasmania]] in the reconstruction of [[Claire Bowern]].<ref name=Bowern>Claire Bowern, September 2012, "The riddle of Tasmanian languages", ''Proc. R. Soc. B'', 279, 4590–4595, doi: 10.1098/rspb.2012.1842</ref> It was spoken along the west coast of the island, from [[Macquarie Harbour]] north to [[Circular Head]] and [[Robbins Island (Tasmania)|Robbins Island]].

Northwestern Tasmanian is poorly attested from four word lists: The "west coast" vocabularies of Charles Robinson and [[George Augustus Robinson]], with 246 words combined; the [[Robbins Island (Tasmania)|Robbins Island]] list of George Augustus Robinson, with 162 words; and the Macquarie Harbour vocabularies of [[Allan Cunningham (botanist)|Allan Cunningham]] (222 words), collected in 1819.<ref>Bowern (2012), supplement</ref>

The list collected by George Augustus Robinson at [[West Point Aboriginal Site|West Point]] ("Western Tribes") is divergent, and falls out as a separate language in Bowern. However, it includes only 28 words, so little can be definitively said.
